title: Introduction to the BetaDanish Package
text: BetaDanish package provides comprehensive suite tools survival reliability analysis using Beta-Danish distribution. Classical lifetime models, Weibull, Gamma, Log-Normal distributions, often limited hazard shape flexibility. typically force hazard rate strictly monotonic , best, unimodal. Beta-Danish distribution overcomes limitations accommodating decreasing, increasing, unimodal (upside-bathtub), bathtub-shaped hazard rates within single, unified four-parameter family. package implements core mathematical functions, robust Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) complete right-censored data, advanced modules Accelerated Failure Time (AFT) regression, cure-rate models, competing risks.

title: Introduction to the BetaDanish Package
text: Beta-Danish distribution constructed applying beta-generated transformation (Eugene et al., 2002) baseline distribution. baseline used two-parameter exponentiated log-logistic distribution. Let ,b,c,k>0a, b, c, k > 0 parameters distribution. * kk scale parameter. * cc baseline shape parameter. * aa bb beta-generator shape parameters controlling skewness tail weight. Cumulative Distribution Function (CDF) given regularized incomplete beta function: F(t)=IG(t)(,b) F(t) = I_{G(t)}(, b)  G(t)=(kt1+kt)cG(t) = \left( \frac{k t}{1 + k t} \right)^c. Probability Density Function (PDF) : f(t)=ckB(,b)(kt)ca−1(1+kt)ca+1[1−(kt1+kt)c]b−1 f(t) = \frac{c k}{B(, b)} \frac{(k t)^{ca - 1}}{(1 + k t)^{ca + 1}} \left[ 1 - \left( \frac{k t}{1 + k t} \right)^c \right]^{b - 1}

title: Introduction to the BetaDanish Package
text: remission dataset contains remission times 128 bladder cancer patients. data exhibits unimodal/decreasing hazard rate. can easily generate publication-quality diagnostic plots:
code: # Load the built-in dataset data("remission", package = "BetaDanish")  # Fit the full 4-parameter model fit_full <- fit_betadanish(survival::Surv(time, status) ~ 1, data = remission) summary(fit_full)  # Fit the 3-parameter submodel (a = 1) fit_sub <- fit_betadanish(survival::Surv(time, status) ~ 1, data = remission, submodel = TRUE)  # Compare the nested models using a Likelihood Ratio Test (LRT) compare_models(fit_full, fit_sub) # Generates Survival, Hazard, Density, P-P, and Q-Q plots plot(fit_full, type = "all")

title: Introduction to the BetaDanish Package
text: many clinical datasets (like transplant data), proportion patients may “cured” never experience event. Standard survival models force survival curve zero, misrepresents data. BetaDanish package provides fit_bd_cure() function fit Mixture Promotion-Time (Non-Mixture) cure models.
code: # Fit a mixture cure model # Latency (time to event for susceptible) has no covariates (~ 1) # Incidence (probability of being susceptible) depends on treatment group (~ group) cure_fit <- fit_bd_cure(   formula_aft = survival::Surv(time, status) ~ 1,   formula_cure = ~ group,   data = transplant,   type = "mixture" )  summary(cure_fit)

what: The Beta-Danish Distribution for Lifetime Data Analysis
title: The Beta-Danish Distribution for Lifetime Data Analysis
text: BetaDanish R package provides comprehensive suite tools survival reliability analysis using highly flexible four-parameter Beta-Danish distribution three-parameter submodel. Developed part doctoral research Department Statistics, Allama Iqbal Open University (AIOU), Islamabad, package addresses limitations classical distributions (like Weibull Gamma) accommodating decreasing, increasing, unimodal, bathtub-shaped hazard rates.

title: The Beta-Danish Distribution for Lifetime Data Analysis
text: Beta-Danish distribution useful classical lifetime models restrictive. provides additional flexibility modeling complex hazard-rate shapes commonly observed survival, reliability, biomedical data.

title: The Beta-Danish Distribution for Lifetime Data Analysis
text: Core Mathematics: Numerically stable implementations density (d), distribution (p), quantile (q), random generation (r), hazard (h) functions. Robust Estimation: Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) engine supporting complete right-censored data via survival::Surv objects. Model Comparison: Automated benchmarking standard lifetime distributions (Weibull, Log-Normal, Log-Logistic, Gamma, Exponential) ranked Goodness--Fit tables. Accelerated Failure Time (AFT) regression. Mixture Promotion-Time (Non-Mixture) Cure Models. Competing Risks analysis assuming independent latent failure times. Publication-Ready Plots: Built-S3 methods plotting survival, hazard, density, P-P, Q-Q plots.
